title: Work, people & everyday life
subtitle: Office life, a coffee-shop conversation, and a misplaced purse.

questions.prompt: ____ I have to sleep with my bedroom window open because our air conditioner doesn't work very well.
questions.explanation: “More often than not” means usually. It describes how frequently the speaker sleeps with the window open.
“Gets along well with” means has a friendly relationship with someone. “Gets” agrees with “he.”
“Am crazy about” means really like or enjoy something. Use “am” with “I.”

questions.prompt: We did a lot. Let's ____ and get some rest.
questions.explanation: “Call it a day” means stop working. They have done a lot and want to rest.

questions.prompt: It's lunchtime. Let's ____ this meeting and go out to eat.
questions.explanation: “Wrap up” means finish or bring to an end. They want to finish the meeting before lunch.

questions.prompt: My father wants to have someone ____ our car engine.
questions.explanation: “Take a look at” means examine or evaluate something. Someone will examine the engine.

questions.prompt: She was too tired to ____ her reading, so she went to bed.
questions.explanation: “Concentrate on” means focus attention on something. She was too tired to focus on her reading.

questions.prompt: Things will ____ well in the end. You just have to be patient.
questions.explanation: “Turn out” describes the final result. The speaker expects things to end well.

questions.prompt: She said that a good education begins at home. She ____.
questions.explanation: “Has a point” means her opinion is reasonable or worth agreeing with.

questions.prompt: Can you help me with this? ____. I see you are busy.
questions.explanation: “Never mind” withdraws the request for help after the speaker notices that the other person is busy.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: How did your date last night ____?
lines.explanation: Alice asks about the result of the date. After “did,” use the base form “turn out.”

lines.speaker: Carol
lines.text: It was O.K. We ____ each other, but I didn't feel any attraction for him.
lines.explanation: They were friendly and comfortable together. “Got” is the past tense of “get.”

lines.speaker: Carol
lines.text: He was a nice guy, but not my type. I ____ a man who spends his whole day with a computer. I prefer someone who is more of a “people person.”
lines.explanation: Carol does not particularly like that type of man. The negative phrase fits her stated preference.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: Computer programmers make a lot of money, Carol.

lines.speaker: Carol
lines.text: You ____, Alice. Actually, he does work for a very large company.
lines.explanation: Carol agrees that Alice has offered a reasonable opinion.

lines.speaker: Carol
lines.text: We took a picture together at one of those funny photo booths. Here, ____ him for yourself.
lines.explanation: Carol invites Alice to look at the photo and form her own opinion.

lines.speaker: Alice
lines.text: That's him? Oh, ____, Carol. You can do better than that!
lines.explanation: Alice drops the earlier favorable suggestion after seeing the photo.

story.title: Idioms in context
paragraphs: I usually get along with everyone at my office. Recently however, the woman who sits across from me bought a new cell phone. She was crazy about it. More often than not, she was chatting with her friends. It was very difficult to concentrate on work. One afternoon, we all decided to call it a day and go out for dinner. However, we made the woman promise not to bring her cell phone into the restaurant. “Do you think you’ll survive without it?” I joked to her. “No problem,” she said.

The evening was fun but it was getting late so we wrapped up dinner and left the restaurant. I was the last to leave and just as I was getting into my car, a waiter came running up to me. “I found this purse at your table!” he said. I took a look at it. “That’s my co-worker’s purse,” I said. “Why don’t you call and leave a message on her answering machine,” the waiter suggested. “You can use the phone in the restaurant.”

We went inside. I was about to dial her home number when I had an idea. “Never mind leaving a message on her machine. I’ll call her cellular phone. That way, she can drive back before she gets all the way home.” “You have a good point!” the waiter said.
When I called her cellular phone, a ringing noise came from her purse. It turned out that her phone was in her purse the whole time!
